classification.difficultyReason: Combine conjugate fifth-power expansions and justify a nearest integer without a calculator.

content.prompt: Expand $(2+\sqrt{3})^5+(2-\sqrt{3})^5$ and hence, find the nearest integer to $(2+\sqrt{3})^5$ without the use of a calculator.

answer.worked:
Use row 5 coefficients $1,5,10,10,5,1$; the odd powers of the negative term change sign.

$$\begin{align*}(2+\sqrt{3})^5&=32+80\sqrt{3}+240+120\sqrt{3}+90+9\sqrt{3}\\(2+\sqrt{3})^5&=362+209\sqrt{3}\\(2-\sqrt{3})^5&=32-80\sqrt{3}+240-120\sqrt{3}+90-9\sqrt{3}\\(2-\sqrt{3})^5&=362-209\sqrt{3}\\(2+\sqrt{3})^5+(2-\sqrt{3})^5&=724\end{align*}$$

Since $\left(\frac32\right)^2<3<2^2$, we have $\frac32<\sqrt{3}<2$. Thus $0<2-\sqrt{3}<\frac12$ and $0<(2-\sqrt{3})^5<\frac1{32}$.

$$\begin{align*}(2+\sqrt{3})^5&=724-(2-\sqrt{3})^5\end{align*}$$

This is less than $\frac1{32}$ below $724$, so its nearest integer is $724$.
